answer.label: Usually traced to
answer.sourceLine: The best-supported version concerns Zhou Enlai, not Mao Zedong. Quote Investigator favors an explanation in which Zhou understood the question to concern the Paris unrest of 1968; the anecdote and its English wording nevertheless vary across retellings.

source.excerpt: It is too early yet to say.
trail: Quote Investigator ↗ traces a related 1939 anecdote and distinguishes it from later versions attached to Mao and Zhou.
Hansard ↗ confirms the 1978 story but names the respondent only as a Chinese representative.
source.rightsNote: The compact English wording belongs to several modern retellings, not an identified original translation or cleared speech transcript. No public-domain status is asserted.

author.name: Zhou Enlai
author.heading: About Zhou Enlai
author.bio: Zhou Enlai was the People’s Republic of China’s first premier, serving from 1949 until his death. His diplomatic role makes him a plausible participant in this story, but it does not turn every later retelling into a transcript.

cite.sourceCitation: Best-available chronology: Quote Investigator. “Dialogue Origin: What Has Been the Impact of the French Revolution? It’s Too Early To Tell.” April 2, 2025. See also Lord Chalfont, House of Lords, December 6, 1978.
cite.pageCitation: Quotle.info. “Who really said ‘It’s too early to tell’?” Last verified 9 Nov 2026.

copyAttribution: Usually attributed in this anecdote to Zhou Enlai; the Mao credit is unsupported, and the exact English wording and original exchange remain uncertain.

misattribution.heading: Often misattributed
misattribution.intro: The same reply travels with different speakers and different supposed meetings.

items.why: QI’s comparison ↗ finds Mao’s role unlikely and favors Zhou Enlai.

misattribution.truthLine: Zhou is the better-supported reported speaker; the exact English sentence remains a retelling, not a stenographic quotation.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The familiar story makes a Chinese statesman seem to judge the French Revolution on a centuries-long timescale. QI’s better-supported explanation is less mystical: Zhou was thinking about the recent Paris upheaval of 1968, while his questioner meant the revolution of 1789.

schema.claimReviewed: Mao Zedong gave the reply “It’s too early to tell” when asked about the French Revolution.
schema.faqAnswer: Mao Zedong’s authorship is not confirmed. The best-supported account favors Zhou Enlai, and both the subject of the question and the exact English wording vary in retellings.
schema.verdictNote: QI favors Zhou Enlai as the reported speaker but does not establish a verbatim Mao quotation.
